name: Wide Creator 4-4-2

slots.why: The sweeper keeper supports a higher engagement line and starts short combinations.
The support full-back overlaps selectively behind the defensive winger and keeps that flank secure.
A conventional defender anchors the back four; Cover is available for a quicker player.
The ball-playing defender can switch play toward the wide creator.
The attacking wing-back overlaps the playmaker, supplying the width the role deliberately gives up.
The defensive winger works back to protect the left and presses the opposition full-back, allowing the opposite flank to attack.
The defensive midfielder holds the centre and covers when the right-back overlaps.
The supporting midfielder links the central pair with the playmaker and forwards.
The wide playmaker drifts inside to create from the right, freeing the flank for the wing-back.
The deep-lying forward connects the wide creator with the runner beside him.
The advanced forward attacks the space created by the playmaker and overlapping wing-back.

description: A 4-4-2 with a defensive winger securing one flank and an attacking wide playmaker creating from the other, supported by an overlap and complementary forwards.
whyGood: It finds a role for a technical wide midfielder without exposing both flanks, and gives a fast striker runners to chase beyond the creator.
whyThisShape: The left side forms a defensive working unit, while the right side is deliberately overloaded: the playmaker comes inside, the wing-back overlaps, and the supporting striker offers a short connection. The central midfield pair keeps the asymmetry from becoming an open midfield.
whenToUse: When one of your best creators is a natural ML/MR rather than an attacking winger, and you have a tireless defensive wide player to balance him.
whenNotToUse: Against a side that can overload the space behind the attacking right-back, or if the wide playmaker lacks the technical quality to justify the imbalance.

instructionRationale.Fairly Wide: Give the wide outlets space to receive and stretch the opponent without isolating every central passer.
instructionRationale.Slightly Shorter Passing: Retain connected passing options while still allowing progression into the forward line.
instructionRationale.Work Ball Into Box: Look for an opening around the penalty area rather than encouraging speculative shots.
instructionRationale.Overlap Right: Ask the right-sided receiver to consider the outside run; this requires a wide defender who can supply that run.
instructionRationale.Counter-Press: Challenge immediately after losing possession, with the roles around the ball supporting the first pressure.
instructionRationale.Higher Line of Engagement: Engage the build-up earlier, accepting that the forwards need support from the midfield behind them.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: Keep the back line at its mentality-relative default rather than explicitly pushing it up or dropping it.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Centre Backs: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Low Crosses: A starting delivery choice for the receiving roles, to review against the actual forwards.
instructionRationale.More Urgent Pressing: Challenge more often inside the selected engagement zone without making the settled press maximal.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Take Short Kicks: Start possession through the chosen short outlets instead of routinely contesting a long kick.

setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
